thread:
Incident Bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: High latency (p99 > 5s) for customer ElkBench on hosted cluster us-west-2. 3 alerts in last 5m. Paging Ryan (oncall).

Ryan (oncall): grabbing it. seeing p95 ~ 600ms but p99 spikes to 6-9s on streaming endpoints. anyone else seeing this?

Maya SRE: I'm on traces. Most of the p99s are streaming stalls stuck at 'open_stream' on gateway for ~5-8s. origin looks like single-tenant pool elkbench-prod-1.

Ali (runtime): curious — model kernels look fine on GPU. no queueing on GPUs, token throughput steady. Could be preproc or request fan-in.

Julian (support): Lena, ElkBench ops pinged support saying they started a new job ~10m ago, sending batched prompts via the streaming API. They report occasional timeouts in their UI.

Lena (CS): Confirmed. ElkBench Ops: can you paste a sample prompt (redact PII)?

ElkBench Ops (external): paste from customer: "<REDACTED BLOB>". They said they switched on gzip for payloads to save bandwidth a few minutes ago.

Sam (infra): gzip on the API gateway is handled by our ingest layer (unpack -> validate -> tokenize). If payloads are large compressed objects that expand to huge token counts, tokenization + KV cache ops could blow up CPU and memory.

Maya SRE: I pulled a flamegraph from ingress. There's a big CPU spike inside tokenization and utf8-normalization. Some requests show token counts > 250k after decompression. That explains stalls while we allocate KV cache and do prefix processing.

Ali (runtime): 250k tokens is bad — our KV cache was being populated/prefixed per request which causes long prefix build time and kvcache eviction thrash for single-tenant pool. That explains p99 tail but not median.

Ryan (oncall): mitigation plan: 1) temporarily throttle concurrency for elkbench-prod-1 to 4 concurrent streams; 2) block gzip at the gateway for that customer (force 415 on compressed content); 3) if needed move traffic to dedicated fallback pool with higher memory. Thoughts?

Maya SRE: +1. Throttling first is lowest risk. I'll update routing policy to cap concurrency. Running command: 
```
rdwctl routing set-concurrency --pool elkbench-prod-1 --limit 4 --reason "p99 stall mitigation"
```

Incident Bot: Change applied by Maya SRE. New concurrency limit 4 for elkbench-prod-1.

Ryan (oncall): Noted. Sam, can we add a temporary content filter to reject compressed content for that customer?

Sam (infra): We can add a quick filter rule on the edge: if Content-Encoding: gzip and owner=elkbench then return 415 + body explaining to disable gzip. Pushing patch to edge config now.

Sam (infra): Patch deployed to edge for us-west-2. Rule: 415 if compressed and owner tag elkbench.

Incident Bot: Edge rule deployed by Sam (infra).

ElkBench Ops (external): We can disable gzip on our side immediately while you continue to investigate. We're toggling it off now.

Julian (support): customer confirms gzip off. I'm going to monitor their client errors and UX.

Maya SRE: After throttling and disabling gzip, p99 dropped to ~1.2s within 90s. Some residual stalls at 2-3s likely from in-flight large requests finishing.

Ali (runtime): Good. Next step: add a detector to reject/slow-path requests with expanded token count > 50k to avoid future blowups. We should also add a hard cap for single-request tokenization at 100k.

Ryan (oncall): Agreed. Can we do a quick prod-safe gate: if expand_tokens > 100k then 413 Payload Too Large with guidance?

Sam (infra): I can add the gate at the ingress layer. Will schedule a hotfix to apply host-wide for the cluster.

Maya SRE: Also capturing samples for postmortem: example requests, flamegraphs, and kvcache eviction logs. Saving to /var/incident/1769004321/ for the team.

ElkBench Ops (external): We're running a job that creates long multi-document prompts. We'll audit and change batching. Appreciate the fast response.

Lena (CS): I'll coordinate with the customer to validate changes and get confirmation they're not hitting errors now.

Ryan (oncall): Summary for the page: root cause appears to be compressed payloads that expand to extreme token counts causing tokenization CPU spikes and KV cache thrash in a single-tenant pool. Immediate mitigations: concurrency cap, block gzip for that customer, apply expanded-token gate. Recovery: p99 reduced to acceptable levels.

Maya SRE: Adding on-call handoff note: I'll keep monitoring for 30m then hand to next SRE on shift if stable.

Incident Bot: :white_check_mark: Incident acknowledged resolved->monitoring. Paging done.

Ryan (oncall): Thanks team. Postmortem owner assigned: Maya SRE. Please pick action items: ingress gating, ticket to runtime to hard-cap per-request tokenization, and CS follow-up with ElkBench.

Maya SRE: Will file the postmortem and action items.

Julian (support): I'll follow up with the customer on observed errors and recommended client-side changes.

ElkBench Ops (external): Confirm no more UI timeouts after disabling gzip. Thanks all.

Ryan (oncall): closing thread in 1h if green.
